title: Role adjacency and compact role contracts for multitenant permission lattice
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define a compact, adjacency-based role contract model that maps tenant-scoped resources into a normalized permission lattice. The goal is to replace ad-hoc role blobs with composable role contracts that are easy to reason about, efficiently checkable in the runtime path, and auditable for security reviews. This ticket covers the design, example matrices, migration strategy from v1 roles, and required console/admin guardrails.
background: Current RBAC (v1) uses monolithic role objects per workspace with implicit inheritance and special-case admin flags. This has caused unclear escalation paths, expensive runtime checks, and gaps in audit trails when roles are mutated. We need a v2 role model which is explicit about adjacency (which roles can delegate or impersonate), constraints by resource scope, and deny-by-default semantics for safer defaults.
goals: Introduce role contracts: small, composable descriptors of allowed actions, constraints, and delegation edges
Model resources as a hierarchical lattice (org > workspace > dataset > model) and attach scope tokens to contracts
Provide deterministic permission evaluation with O(log N) checks for common paths
Emit rich audit events that capture contract provenance and effective permission decisions
Support SSO/SAML group-to-contract mapping with minimal friction and safe defaults
non_goals: Fully replace all legacy role objects in first rollout (we will support hybrid mode)
Build a complete UI for editing contracts in this ticket (console work is follow-up)
Ship custom policy language — keep predicates simple: attribute-matching and scope intersection
design_summary:
We propose a compact role contract format:

  contract_id: <string>
  actions: [read, write, deploy, manage]
  resource_pattern: org/:org_id/workspace/:ws_id/*  (wildcards allowed)
  constraints: {time_window, ip_allowlist, privilege_exceptions}
  adjacency: [can_delegate_to_contract_id, can_be_delegated_from_contract_id]
  inheritance: explicit list (no implicit parent chaining)

Contracts are small (<= 1KB), normalized, and stored in a tenant-scoped registry. At runtime, request context contains an active list of contract_ids for the principal; permission evaluation is a short-circuit intersection of actions and resource_pattern matches. Delegation is evaluated by adjacency edges (deny-by-default unless adjacency present).
role_contracts:
Example contract (compact form):

  - contract_id: CONTRACT:ws-admin
    actions: [manage, deploy, read, write]
    resource_pattern: org/:org_id/workspace/:ws_id/*
    constraints: []
    adjacency: [CONTRACT:workspace-operator]

  - contract_id: CONTRACT:workspace-operator
    actions: [deploy, read]
    resource_pattern: org/:org_id/workspace/:ws_id/models/*
    constraints: [time_window=09:00-18:00]
    adjacency: []

Adjacency example: ws-admin -> workspace-operator (admin can delegate to operator for temporary escalation).
resource_hierarchy_example:
Canonical resource path segments used across platform:

  org/:org_id
  org/:org_id/workspace/:ws_id
  org/:org_id/workspace/:ws_id/dataset/:dataset_id
  org/:org_id/workspace/:ws_id/model/:model_id

Scopes attach at any segment. Contracts either declare an exact pattern or use trailing wildcard. Scope intersection rules: a contract applies if its pattern intersects request path.
permission_matrix_sample:
ASCII permission matrix (example):

  ACTION      | CONTRACT:viewer | CONTRACT:editor | CONTRACT:operator | CONTRACT:ws-admin
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  read        | allow           | allow            | allow             | allow
  write       | deny            | allow            | deny              | allow
  deploy      | deny            | deny             | allow             | allow
  manage      | deny            | deny             | deny              | allow

Note: evaluation is 'first applicable' by contract priority; otherwise explicit allow/deny with deny overriding allows in same decision set.
admin_controls: Canary delegation: time-limited adjacency edges that auto-expire (default 24h)
Two-person approval required to create adjacency that grants 'manage' across org boundaries
Admin-safe mode: top-level org-admin cannot be deleted or demoted without exportable audit bundle
Console preview: show effective contracts and resource intersections before applying changes
audit_logging_changes: Emit 'permission-evaluation' event with: principal_id, active_contracts, requested_action, resource_path, decision, matched_contracts
Log contract mutations with prior_state, delta, actor, reason, request_id
Link SSO mapping events (group-sync) to resulting assigned contract_ids in audit stream
Store a hash of contract definitions in per-tenant audit index for tamper-evidence
sso_saml_mapping: Mapping approach: SAML group -> contract assignment rule. Rules are tenant-configurable and evaluated during SSO session issuance. Default mapping is conservative (groups map to viewer-equivalent contracts). Group claims can provision temporary contracts (session-scoped) rather than persistent assignments to reduce stale privileges. For complex orgs, allow attribute-based mapping (e.g., department=infra -> CONTRACT:workspace-operator).
migration_plan: Phase 1 (compat mode): support v1 role blobs by translating to best-effort contract sets at read-time; do not mutate v1 roles
Phase 2 (export/import): provide a tool to export v1 role mappings and suggest contract candidates with adjacency suggestions
Phase 3 (opt-in): allow tenants to opt into contract registry and start issuing session-scoped contracts via SSO mapping
Phase 4 (enforce): deprecate fallback checks and require contracts for all permission checks (release rbac-v2.0)
acceptance_criteria: Permission evaluation tests that cover 95% of existing access patterns and run within 1.5x current median latency for common paths
Audit events emitted for every contract mutation and permission decision (test harness validating schema)
SSO group-to-contract mapping POC completed and documented with example configs
Migration tool produces suggested contract assignments for at least 80% of v1 roles with low manual edits

Proto runtime evaluator implementation with caching (owner: Marco Li, 5d)

open_questions: Should adjacency be directional only, or also support symmetric delegation shortcuts?
What is an acceptable default expiration for time-limited delegations (24h vs 7d)?
How to handle cross-tenant shared resources (partner integrations) in the contract registry?
Do we need a compact binary representation for contracts to reduce storage/IO costs?
decisions: Adopt deny-by-default semantics with explicit adjacency required for delegation
Store contracts in tenant-scoped registry with exportable hashes for auditability
SSO mapping will default to session-scoped temporary contracts unless tenant opts for persistent assignments
